title: Flash-Loan Governance
summary: A governor holds a treasury and can execute a proposal when the caller has a supermajority of votes. Voting power deposited in the same transaction must not count toward that supermajority. A depositor whose votes were already checkpointed can still execute, and ordinary deposits and withdrawals must keep working.

realWorld.incident: Beanstalk Farms governance exploit, Ethereum, 2022-04-17 about 12:24 UTC
realWorld.lossReported: Beanstalk reported about $77M of non-Bean user assets stolen. Elliptic reported the attacker obtained about $76M (just under 25,000 ETH) and that the protocol lost about $182M in value. Immunefi describes an about $181M incident of which about $77M was non-Bean assets.
realWorld.rootCause: emergencyCommit executed a proposal immediately once the caller held at least two-thirds of live Stalk. Stalk could be borrowed and deposited in that same transaction, so a flash loan was enough to pass and execute.
realWorld.note: Minimal reproduction of same-transaction supermajority execution. The real BIP also had a one-day delay before emergencyCommit; the delay does not stop a flash loan at execution time, so this model keeps the live-vote bug and omits the unrelated delay. Re-implemented from the public post-mortems. The DeFiHackLabs PoC is MIT and is cited only; none of its code is copied.
